method: Independent official-source research; coordinates with scope=area or corridor are reference points, never invented individual parking pads. Website verification is performed by the parent QA run.

candidates.name: Dubinky Well Road — marked primitive camping sites
candidates.scope: corridor-search-area; coordinate is the road access reference, not an individual legal campsite
candidates.coordinateSource: Utah State University 2025 Moab orientation guide; BLM independently confirms the named road's marked-site camping policy
candidates.carEvidence: Official BLM maps describe designated primitive sites, posted parking boundaries and vehicle travel; public-road permission does not permit arbitrary roadside sleeping.

rules.sleeping: Use only a brown-post/tent-symbol designated primitive site; do not camp at the coordinate simply because it marks road access.
rules.fee: Official BLM camping map identifies designated primitive sites as free; separate paid Lone Mesa Group Sites are not this recommendation.
rules.permit: No ordinary overnight permit stated in reviewed Moab sources.
rules.stayLimit: 14 days at one location, then relocate at least 30 miles.
rules.waste: Carry out solid human waste; portable toilet required where no constructed toilet provided.
rules.vehicleAccess: Road access reference is about21.6miles from Moab; USU describes2WD on main routes, highclearance/4WD on secondary routes. No general passenger-car guarantee for every marked site.
rules.fires: No woodcutting or gathering; obey current fire restrictions.

validity.policy: Current BLM recreation page plus2024visitor map/guide, older official georeferenced map for marked-site detail
validity.geometryGap: No verified public vector camping-zone/site geometry found. Do not paint corridor entirely green.

candidates.operatingStatus: No closure found in reviewed current policy sources; per-site occupancy and road-condition availability unknown.

candidates.name: Cinder Hills Off Highway Vehicle Area
candidates.scope: official recreation-area reference point; no claim that every acre or entrance pullout permits camping
candidates.carEvidence: Official live USFS page lists OHV Camping and vehicle access via FR776; official2025travel map identifies Cinder Hills as designated motorized open area. The general forest-road camping rule is not used as sole evidence.

rules.sleeping: Use the designated motorized recreation/camping area beyond any posted no-camping entrance area; no individual pad invented.
rules.fee: No fee stated on current official page; do not label a paid campground.
rules.permit: No ordinary overnight camping permit is stated on the current official page.
rules.stayLimit: 14 days in any consecutive 30 days under order 03-04-00-26-08.
rules.vehicleAccess: 13 miles northeast of downtown Flagstaff, reached by FR 776 from US 89. The November 23 road status lists FR 776 open. Loose cinders and rough roads mean passenger-car access is not guaranteed everywhere.
rules.other: No glass containers. Nearby Sunset Crater National Monument and Strawberry Crater Wilderness closed to OHV travel.

validity.stayOrderEnd: 2028-10-29 per implementation text; the page header conflicts with October 26

candidates.operatingStatus: Official siteOpen and FR776Open; no availability/occupancy guarantee.

candidates.name: West Sedona — eight designated dispersed camping areas
candidates.scope: official reference point for eight named areas, not an exact campsite; separate Sedona subcase, farther than30roadmiles fromFlagstaff
candidates.carEvidence: USFS signed-order exhibit locates roadside dispersed areas Rockview, Angel Valley, Javelina, Surprise, Windmill, Cockscomb, Greasy Spoon, Nolan alongFR525/89B/152A system; these named areas are express camping-ban exceptions.

rules.sleeping: Camp only inside one of the eight designated areas; arbitraryFR525roadside pullouts prohibited within the wider order area.
rules.permit: No reservation required; first come, first served.
rules.stayLimit: 14 days; the forestwide limit of 14 days in any 30 days also applies.
rules.vehicleAccess: FR 525 between SR 89A and FR 152C was listed open November 23. This does not guarantee every inner spur is suitable for a passenger car.
rules.fires: No wood or charcoal fires at any time; LPG stoves and grills with an on/off control are permitted.

candidates.operatingStatus: The official recreation page says Site Open; FR 525 is open. The November Red Rock flood alert does not list this site as closed.

candidates.name: Jean/Roach Dry Lakes — BLM dispersed recreation area
candidates.scope: official recreation-area reference point; broad search area, not a surveyed individual pullout
candidates.carEvidence: BLM lists dispersed camping as an activity, publishes coordinates and driving directions, and distinguishes motorized travel on the lakebed from existing roads and trails outside it.

rules.sleeping: Dispersed camping is an official listed use of this recreation area.
rules.fee: No camping fee stated on official page; not independently verified as a zero-dollar fee.
rules.permit: No ordinary overnight permit is stated on the official page.
rules.stayLimit: 14 days in any 28 days; then people and property must relocate outside a 25-mile radius, or to land not managed by BLM, for 14 days.
rules.vehicleAccess: Official directions place this area about 26 miles south of Las Vegas: I-15 Sloan exit 25 to Las Vegas Boulevard, then Knight Ranch Road. Outside the dry lakebed use existing roads and trails only.
rules.weather: After precipitation the lakebed may retain deep water for a long time. BLM advises against driving on it after rain. Ground conditions are separate from camping permission.

validity.policy: Live official BLM location and Southern Nevada District pages; no blanket permission inferred from land ownership

candidates.operatingStatus: The official page lists dispersed camping. Current ground conditions and occupancy are unknown; no closure was identified on the reviewed page.
